articles.title: (W.E. Talk) James Laurenceson: Australia must remain as deeply connected to China as possible
articles.titleCn: （W.E.对话）詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：澳大利亚必须尽可能与中国保持紧密联系
articles.summary: In recent years, Australia-China relations have continued to improve and develop, with trade and people-to-people exchanges giving important impetus to the development of bilateral relations. Yet challenges remain to deepening cooperation, including geopolitical tensions, differences in strategic perceptions and issues surrounding research collaboration.
articles.summaryCn: 澳大利亚经济学家詹姆斯·劳伦斯森在专访中强调，澳中两国经济高度互补，澳大利亚应尽最大可能与中国保持接触与合作，以维护自身利益并保持在技术前沿。

paragraphs.en: (CNS) -- In recent years, Australia-China relations have continued to improve and develop, with trade and people-to-people exchanges giving important impetus to the development of bilateral relations. Yet challenges remain to deepening cooperation, including geopolitical tensions, differences in strategic perceptions and issues surrounding research collaboration. How can the two countries enhance mutual understanding, expand common ground and manage differences to translate their complementary strengths into further tangible outcomes? In a recent interview with China News Service's “W.E. Talk”, Australian economist James Laurenceson, Director of the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney, highlighted the deep {{0}} between the two countries.
paragraphs.cn: （中新社）——近年来，澳中关系持续改善和发展，贸易和人文交流为双边关系发展提供了重要动力。然而，深化合作仍面临挑战，包括地缘政治紧张、战略认知差异以及研究合作相关问题。两国如何增进相互理解、扩大共同利益、管控分歧，将互补优势转化为更多实实在在的成果？在近日接受中国新闻社“W.E.对话”采访时，澳大利亚经济学家、悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究院院长詹姆斯·劳伦斯森强调了两国之间的深度互补性。

paragraphs.en:
“We have to remain as deeply connected to China as we possibly can,” he said, stressing that Australia needs to engage and cooperate with China to the maximum extent possible and do “whatever we can to be part of China’s development.”
Here are excerpts from the interview:
CNS: In recent years, the Australia-China relationship has returned to a track of steady improvement and development. How do you view the underlying drivers and the future prospects of this relationship? James Laurenceson: I’m cautiously optimistic. I don't think either side wants to return to the {{1}} state of the Australia-China relationship between 2020 and 2022. I also think the approach to the relationship is quite positive and very realistic.
paragraphs.cn: “我们必须尽可能与中国保持紧密联系，”他说，并强调澳大利亚需要最大限度地与中国接触与合作，“尽我们所能参与中国的发展”。以下是采访摘录：中新社：近年来，澳中关系重回稳步改善和发展的轨道。您如何看待这一关系的深层驱动力和未来前景？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：我持谨慎乐观态度。我认为双方都不希望回到2020年至2022年间澳中关系失调的状态。我也认为处理这一关系的方式相当积极且非常务实。

paragraphs.en: Former Chinese ambassador to Australia Xiao Qian was here for four and a half years. He has only just recently returned to Beijing. He often used to say in public that we have differences and we even have disputes. I did not interpret that as a negative. I thought it was positive that he was just being very {{2}}.
paragraphs.cn: 中国前驻澳大利亚大使肖千在澳任职四年半，最近才返回北京。他过去常在公开场合说，我们有分歧，甚至有争端。我并不认为这是负面的。我认为他非常坦率，这是积极的。

paragraphs.en: And he would quickly go on to say that both sides do not want those disputes and differences to {{3}} over to damage areas of mutual cooperation. Both sides recognize that for all the differences, which are real, we have enormous mutual benefits as well. Trade is the obvious one, but not just in trade. When I think about multilateral organizations, for example, both Canberra and Beijing are big supporters of the World Trade Organization and the two sides continue to cooperate. I look forward to seeing further progress in Australia-China cooperation.
paragraphs.cn: 他还会紧接着说，双方都不希望这些争端和分歧蔓延开来，损害共同合作的领域。双方都认识到，尽管分歧确实存在，但我们也有巨大的共同利益。贸易是最明显的，但不仅限于贸易。例如，在多边组织方面，堪培拉和北京都是世界贸易组织的坚定支持者，双方继续开展合作。我期待澳中合作取得进一步进展。

paragraphs.en: CNS: Since its {{4}} in 2014, the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney has maintained very active engagement with Chinese universities and think tanks. In your opinion, what role do people-to-people exchanges, particularly think tank exchanges, play in fostering bilateral relations? James Laurenceson: People-to-people exchanges, especially think tank exchanges, play an important role, and there are bright spots. Scholars and experts meeting at the track two level are able to have more frank discussions. The Australia-China Relations Institute remains very keen on engaging with Chinese delegations coming to Australia.
paragraphs.cn: 中新社：悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究院自2014年成立以来，与中国高校和智库保持着非常活跃的交流。您认为人文交流，特别是智库交流，在促进双边关系中发挥什么作用？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：人文交流，特别是智库交流，发挥着重要作用，也有亮点。学者和专家在二轨层面会晤，能够进行更坦率的讨论。澳中关系研究院仍然非常热衷于与来访澳大利亚的中国代表团接触。

paragraphs.en: And many of our staff, including me, are often in China too. We need to do that because, as much goodwill as there is in the bilateral relationship, {{5}} can arise. For example, one of the views I often encounter in China is that Australia always automatically follows the United States. When I go to China, I can provide examples of many areas where Australia takes a completely different view from that of Washington. I think that different perspective is good for both sides.
paragraphs.cn: 我们的许多员工，包括我本人，也经常去中国。我们需要这样做，因为尽管双边关系中有很多善意，但误解也可能产生。例如，我在中国经常遇到的一种观点是，澳大利亚总是自动跟随美国。我去中国时，可以举出许多澳大利亚与美国持完全不同立场的领域的例子。我认为这种不同的视角对双方都有好处。

paragraphs.en: Trade is the obvious one. Last year, when Donald Trump returned to office, there were some comments coming out of Washington that Washington would prefer that Australia limited or {{6}} its trade relationship with China. The response of Australia's trade minister was to say: “We don’t want to do less business with China; we want to do more business with China. We’ll make decisions about how we continue to engage with China based on our national interests and not on what the Americans may or may not want.” This is a very bold statement from an Australian minister to be making. Another example would be technology issues.
paragraphs.cn: 贸易是最明显的例子。去年唐纳德·特朗普重新执政时，华盛顿传出一些言论，称华盛顿希望澳大利亚限制或削减与中国的贸易关系。澳大利亚贸易部长的回应是：“我们不想减少与中国的生意，我们想增加与中国的生意。我们将根据国家利益来决定如何继续与中国接触，而不是根据美国人可能想要或不想要什么。”这是一位澳大利亚部长非常大胆的表态。另一个例子是技术问题。

paragraphs.en: Australia is very welcoming and completely open to Chinese electric vehicles, batteries and solar products, with zero tariffs on these products. In fact, just this year, China overtook Japan to become Australia's largest supplier of cars, and that was a position that Japan held for nearly three decades. Now our biggest source is China. Similarly, it works in reverse. When Chinese colleagues come to Australia, they can bring views to Australian audiences that those audiences may not have heard before.
paragraphs.cn: 澳大利亚对中国电动汽车、电池和太阳能产品非常欢迎且完全开放，对这些产品征收零关税。事实上，就在今年，中国超越日本成为澳大利亚最大的汽车供应国，而日本占据这一位置近三十年。现在我们最大的来源是中国。同样，反过来也是如此。当中国同事来到澳大利亚时，他们可以给澳大利亚受众带来他们可能从未听过的观点。

paragraphs.en: So it's positive. I would give China some credit for taking steps on the visa-free policy. It's good for Australians traveling to China, obviously, and it's really good for China too. More Australians get to see China firsthand, and that's a good thing. I wish the Australian government would adopt a {{7}} approach, but it has not done so yet.
paragraphs.cn: 所以这是积极的。我要对中国在免签政策上采取的举措表示肯定。这对前往中国的澳大利亚人显然有好处，对中国也确实有好处。更多澳大利亚人能够亲眼看到中国，这是好事。我希望澳大利亚政府能采取对等做法，但迄今尚未这样做。

paragraphs.en: CNS: We noted that in your recent article, you pointed out that Australia risks missing out on access to world-class science and technology by taking an overly {{8}} approach to research collaborations with China. How do you assess the importance of maintaining open sci-tech cooperation between the two nations? James Laurenceson: Open sci-tech cooperation is critical. It's actually more important for Australia than it is for China. China is a large country that has a lot of human talent.
paragraphs.cn: 中新社：我们注意到，您在最近的文章中指出，澳大利亚对与中国的研究合作采取过度限制的做法，有可能错失获得世界一流科学技术的机会。您如何评估两国保持开放科技合作的重要性？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：开放的科技合作至关重要。实际上，这对澳大利亚比对中国更重要。中国是一个大国，拥有大量人才。

paragraphs.en: To be frank, if Australia does not {{9}} with China, China will be fine. China has an enormous domestic pool of human capital right now. Australia is a country with a small population and limited scale, and has always relied more on international collaboration. If you look at the highest quality Australian scientific publications, about 80% of those involve international collaboration. The only way that a country of Australia's size and resources can stay at that international technology {{10}} is by collaborating internationally.
paragraphs.cn: 坦率地说，如果澳大利亚不与中国合作，中国也不会有问题。中国目前拥有庞大的国内人力资本池。澳大利亚人口少、规模有限，一直更依赖国际合作。如果你看澳大利亚最高质量的科学出版物，大约80%涉及国际合作。一个像澳大利亚这样规模和资源的国家，要保持在国际技术前沿，唯一的途径就是开展国际合作。

paragraphs.en: The other side of that is that China’s own innovation systems and talent pool have developed enormously over the last decade. If we cut ourselves off from the world's leading source of global innovation and talent, then that's going to come at a big cost to Australia. That's my concern. CNS: The Australian Foreign Minister asked the Australian National University (ANU) and the University of Queensland (UQ) to terminate their collaboration with Shandong University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, respectively. What's your perspective on this development?
paragraphs.cn: 另一方面，中国的创新体系和人才库在过去十年中发展巨大。如果我们与世界上领先的创新和人才来源隔绝，那将给澳大利亚带来巨大代价。这就是我的担忧。中新社：澳大利亚外长要求澳大利亚国立大学和昆士兰大学分别终止与山东大学和中国科学院的合作。您如何看待这一事态？

paragraphs.en: James Laurenceson: I've been watching those two news stories very closely. There may well be relevant information behind the decision-making that I am not {{11}} to, but I can make two points. First of all, at least on the surface, they don't seem to be particularly risky deals. For example, the deal between Shandong University and the Australian National University was mostly about undergraduate teaching. There wasn't even a research component.
paragraphs.cn: 詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：我一直在密切关注这两则新闻。决策背后可能有我不了解的相关信息，但我可以谈两点。首先，至少从表面上看，这些交易似乎并不特别有风险。例如，山东大学与澳大利亚国立大学的协议主要是关于本科教学，甚至没有研究部分。

paragraphs.en: So it's not at all clear to me how that threatened Australia's interests or national security. And similarly, the deal with UQ wasn't a particularly risky deal either. So I think it's generated a lot of confusion. Secondly, the impact of that will be that many other universities and academics will be looking at what's happened and just coming to their own assessments of what went wrong. They will be {{12}} to forge new collaborative agreements with China because they're worried that if they put in all this work and engage with the Chinese partner with goodwill and in good faith, and then the deal gets cancelled, the Australian university will be left in a big mess, and so will the Chinese partner.
paragraphs.cn: 所以我不清楚这如何威胁到澳大利亚的利益或国家安全。同样，与昆士兰大学的协议也不是特别有风险的交易。所以我认为这引发了很多困惑。其次，其影响将是许多其他大学和学者会关注发生的事情，并自行评估出了什么问题。他们将不愿与中国缔结新的合作协议，因为他们担心，如果他们投入所有这些工作，以善意和诚信与中国伙伴接触，然后协议被取消，澳大利亚大学将陷入巨大混乱，中国伙伴也是如此。

paragraphs.en: The two sides probably won't even try. I think that's the risk. CNS: How do you view the opportunities for Australia-China cooperation in the green sector, particularly in clean energy and new energy vehicles? How can both countries join forces to advance the green economy and strengthen green cooperation? James Laurenceson: As in so many other areas of the Australia-China economic relationship, the two countries just have deep complementarities.
paragraphs.cn: 双方可能甚至不会尝试。我认为这就是风险所在。中新社：您如何看待澳中在绿色领域，特别是清洁能源和新能源汽车方面的合作机遇？两国如何携手推进绿色经济、加强绿色合作？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：正如澳中经济关系的许多其他领域一样，两国就是有着深度的互补性。

paragraphs.en: This is why Australia and China's economic and trade engagement is so strong. Just to give a few examples from the green space: Australia is a major global supplier of lithium, and China is its largest export market for lithium ore. Chinese electric vehicles are very popular in Australia, as are home battery systems and solar panels. There are things that both sides could do to take it to an even higher level. If I were advising the Australian government, I would urge it to be more open towards Chinese investment in Australia, particularly in the renewable energy space.
paragraphs.cn: 这就是澳中经贸往来如此强劲的原因。仅举绿色领域的几个例子：澳大利亚是全球主要的锂供应国，中国是其最大的锂矿石出口市场。中国电动汽车在澳大利亚非常受欢迎，家用电池系统和太阳能电池板也是如此。双方可以采取一些措施将其提升到更高水平。如果我为澳大利亚政府提供建议，我会敦促其对中国在澳投资更加开放，特别是在可再生能源领域。

paragraphs.en: Over the last five years, the Australian government has taken a stricter approach towards Chinese investment, particularly in certain sectors like critical minerals. I can't think of one investment in that sector that has been approved over the last five years. I think that's a mistake. That's going too far in the security direction, and it could potentially bring significant economic costs. Australia can get investment capital from many countries.
paragraphs.cn: 过去五年，澳大利亚政府对中国投资采取了更严格的做法，特别是在关键矿产等某些领域。我想不出过去五年中该领域有哪一项投资获得批准。我认为这是一个错误。这在安全方向上走得太远了，可能带来重大经济代价。澳大利亚可以从许多国家获得投资资本。

paragraphs.en: It's not hard, but Chinese companies these days are often the world's technology leaders as well. And that's the thing about foreign investment: it's not just the dollars; it's also the technology that often comes bundled with that foreign investment. I think it would be very unfortunate for Australia's interests if we blocked Chinese investment outright. There is also a question of whether Beijing would allow a Chinese company to take its best technology to a place like Australia. We know these sorts of technology exports are {{13}} much more closely than in the past as economic exchanges have become more {{14}}.
paragraphs.cn: 这并不难，但中国企业如今往往也是世界技术领导者。这就是外国投资的特点：不仅仅是美元，通常还捆绑着技术。我认为，如果我们完全阻止中国投资，对澳大利亚的利益将非常不利。还有一个问题是，北京是否允许中国公司将其最好的技术带到澳大利亚这样的地方。我们知道，随着经济交流日益安全化，这类技术出口比过去受到更严格的审查。

paragraphs.en: In fact, China is ahead of Australia in areas such as artificial intelligence and robotics. And even in fundamental scientific research, China now produces more of the world’s best fundamental scientific publications than the US. It’s very impressive. As an Australian, I do my best to raise awareness in Australia about the reality of the world in 2026. If Australia wants to stay at that technology frontier, we have to remain as deeply connected to China as we possibly can.
paragraphs.cn: 事实上，中国在人工智能和机器人等领域领先于澳大利亚。即使在基础科学研究方面，中国现在产生的世界最佳基础科学出版物也比美国多。这非常令人印象深刻。作为澳大利亚人，我尽我所能提高澳大利亚人对2026年世界现实的认识。如果澳大利亚想保持在技术前沿，我们必须尽可能与中国保持紧密联系。

paragraphs.en: I understand that every country has to protect its national security, but my view is that Australia needs to be engaged with China to the maximum extent possible. CNS: The upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, China, and Australian Prime Minister Albanese will travel to China to attend. How do you view the opportunities for cooperation within the APEC framework? James Laurenceson: The good thing about Australia and China is that when it comes to trade, which is primarily what APEC is about in terms of broader economic cooperation, the two countries are actually quite {{15}}. More trade and more economic integration aren't just good for prosperity; they're good for stability and security too.
paragraphs.cn: 我理解每个国家都必须保护其国家安全，但我的观点是，澳大利亚需要最大限度地与中国接触。中新社：即将举行的亚太经合组织领导人非正式会议将在中国深圳举行，澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯将赴华出席。您如何看待亚太经合组织框架内的合作机遇？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：澳大利亚和中国的好处在于，在贸易方面——这基本上是亚太经合组织更广泛经济合作的主要内容——两国实际上相当一致。更多贸易和更深入的经济一体化不仅有利于繁荣，也有利于稳定和安全。

paragraphs.en: So that's a great starting point. If a majority of APEC members take the opportunity at the November meeting in Shenzhen to simply signal that they remain committed to open and free global markets, I think that's a positive outcome.n is an economist, educator, analyst and researcher. He is Director of the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney. Professor Laurenceson conducts research that seeks to inform Australia’s engagement with China. His research has been published in leading scholarly journals including China Economic Review, China Economic Journal, Journal of Contemporary China and Australian Journal of International Affairs.
paragraphs.cn: 所以这是一个很好的起点。如果大多数亚太经合组织成员利用11月深圳会议的机会， simply表明他们仍然致力于开放和自由的全球市场，我认为这是一个积极的成果。劳伦斯森是一位经济学家、教育家、分析师和研究员。他是悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究院院长。劳伦斯森教授开展研究，旨在为澳大利亚与中国的接触提供参考。他的研究成果发表在《中国经济评论》《中国经济杂志》《当代中国杂志》和《澳大利亚国际事务杂志》等领先学术期刊上。

paragraphs.en: Professor Laurenceson also provides regular commentary on contemporary developments in China’s economy and the Australia-China relationship. His opinion articles have appeared in The Australian Financial Review, The Australian, The Sydney Morning Herald, South China Morning Post, among many other publications.
paragraphs.cn: 劳伦斯森教授还定期就中国经济和澳中关系的当代发展发表评论。他的评论文章发表在《澳大利亚金融评论》《澳大利亚人报》《悉尼先驱晨报》《南华早报》等众多出版物上。

(CNS) -- In recent years, Australia-China relations have continued to improve and develop, with trade and people-to-people exchanges giving important impetus to the development of bilateral relations. Yet challenges remain to deepening cooperation, including geopolitical tensions, differences in strategic perceptions and issues surrounding research collaboration.
How can the two countries enhance mutual understanding, expand common ground and manage differences to translate their complementary strengths into further tangible outcomes?
In a recent interview with China News Service's “W.E. Talk”, Australian economist James Laurenceson, Director of the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney, highlighted the deep complementarities between the two countries. “We have to remain as deeply connected to China as we possibly can,” he said, stressing that Australia needs to engage and cooperate with China to the maximum extent possible and do “whatever we can to be part of China’s development.”
Here are excerpts from the interview:
CNS: In recent years, the Australia-China relationship has returned to a track of steady improvement and development. How do you view the underlying drivers and the future prospects of this relationship?
James Laurenceson: I’m cautiously optimistic. I don't think either side wants to return to the dysfunctional state of the Australia-China relationship between 2020 and 2022.
I also think the approach to the relationship is quite positive and very realistic. Former Chinese ambassador to Australia Xiao Qian was here for four and a half years. He has only just recently returned to Beijing. He often used to say in public that we have differences and we even have disputes. I did not interpret that as a negative. I thought it was positive that he was just being very frank. And he would quickly go on to say that both sides do not want those disputes and differences to spill over to damage areas of mutual cooperation.
Both sides recognize that for all the differences, which are real, we have enormous mutual benefits as well. Trade is the obvious one, but not just in trade. When I think about multilateral organizations, for example, both Canberra and Beijing are big supporters of the World Trade Organization and the two sides continue to cooperate. I look forward to seeing further progress in Australia-China cooperation.
CNS: Since its inception in 2014, the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney has maintained very active engagement with Chinese universities and think tanks. In your opinion, what role do people-to-people exchanges, particularly think tank exchanges, play in fostering bilateral relations?
James Laurenceson: People-to-people exchanges, especially think tank exchanges, play an important role, and there are bright spots. Scholars and experts meeting at the track two level are able to have more frank discussions. The Australia-China Relations Institute remains very keen on engaging with Chinese delegations coming to Australia. And many of our staff, including me, are often in China too.
We need to do that because, as much goodwill as there is in the bilateral relationship, misconceptions can arise. For example, one of the views I often encounter in China is that Australia always automatically follows the United States. When I go to China, I can provide examples of many areas where Australia takes a completely different view from that of Washington. I think that different perspective is good for both sides.
Trade is the obvious one. Last year, when Donald Trump returned to office, there were some comments coming out of Washington that Washington would prefer that Australia limited or curtailed its trade relationship with China.
The response of Australia's trade minister was to say: “We don’t want to do less business with China; we want to do more business with China. We’ll make decisions about how we continue to engage with China based on our national interests and not on what the Americans may or may not want.” This is a very bold statement from an Australian minister to be making.
Another example would be technology issues. Australia is very welcoming and completely open to Chinese electric vehicles, batteries and solar products, with zero tariffs on these products. In fact, just this year, China overtook Japan to become Australia's largest supplier of cars, and that was a position that Japan held for nearly three decades. Now our biggest source is China.
Similarly, it works in reverse. When Chinese colleagues come to Australia, they can bring views to Australian audiences that those audiences may not have heard before. So it's positive.
I would give China some credit for taking steps on the visa-free policy. It's good for Australians traveling to China, obviously, and it's really good for China too. More Australians get to see China firsthand, and that's a good thing.
I wish the Australian government would adopt a reciprocal approach, but it has not done so yet.
CNS: We noted that in your recent article, you pointed out that Australia risks missing out on access to world-class science and technology by taking an overly restrictive approach to research collaborations with China. How do you assess the importance of maintaining open sci-tech cooperation between the two nations?
James Laurenceson: Open sci-tech cooperation is critical. It's actually more important for Australia than it is for China. China is a large country that has a lot of human talent. To be frank, if Australia does not collaborate with China, China will be fine.
China has an enormous domestic pool of human capital right now. Australia is a country with a small population and limited scale, and has always relied more on international collaboration.
If you look at the highest quality Australian scientific publications, about 80% of those involve international collaboration. The only way that a country of Australia's size and resources can stay at that international technology frontier is by collaborating internationally.
The other side of that is that China’s own innovation systems and talent pool have developed enormously over the last decade. If we cut ourselves off from the world's leading source of global innovation and talent, then that's going to come at a big cost to Australia. That's my concern.
CNS: The Australian Foreign Minister asked the Australian National University (ANU) and the University of Queensland (UQ) to terminate their collaboration with Shandong University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, respectively. What's your perspective on this development?
James Laurenceson: I've been watching those two news stories very closely. There may well be relevant information behind the decision-making that I am not privy to, but I can make two points.
First of all, at least on the surface, they don't seem to be particularly risky deals. For example, the deal between Shandong University and the Australian National University was mostly about undergraduate teaching. There wasn't even a research component. So it's not at all clear to me how that threatened Australia's interests or national security.
And similarly, the deal with UQ wasn't a particularly risky deal either. So I think it's generated a lot of confusion.
Secondly, the impact of that will be that many other universities and academics will be looking at what's happened and just coming to their own assessments of what went wrong. They will be reluctant to forge new collaborative agreements with China because they're worried that if they put in all this work and engage with the Chinese partner with goodwill and in good faith, and then the deal gets cancelled, the Australian university will be left in a big mess, and so will the Chinese partner. The two sides probably won't even try. I think that's the risk.
CNS: How do you view the opportunities for Australia-China cooperation in the green sector, particularly in clean energy and new energy vehicles? How can both countries join forces to advance the green economy and strengthen green cooperation?
James Laurenceson: As in so many other areas of the Australia-China economic relationship, the two countries just have deep complementarities. This is why Australia and China's economic and trade engagement is so strong.
Just to give a few examples from the green space: Australia is a major global supplier of lithium, and China is its largest export market for lithium ore. Chinese electric vehicles are very popular in Australia, as are home battery systems and solar panels.
There are things that both sides could do to take it to an even higher level. If I were advising the Australian government, I would urge it to be more open towards Chinese investment in Australia, particularly in the renewable energy space.
Over the last five years, the Australian government has taken a stricter approach towards Chinese investment, particularly in certain sectors like critical minerals. I can't think of one investment in that sector that has been approved over the last five years. I think that's a mistake. That's going too far in the security direction, and it could potentially bring significant economic costs.
Australia can get investment capital from many countries. It's not hard, but Chinese companies these days are often the world's technology leaders as well. And that's the thing about foreign investment: it's not just the dollars; it's also the technology that often comes bundled with that foreign investment. I think it would be very unfortunate for Australia's interests if we blocked Chinese investment outright.
There is also a question of whether Beijing would allow a Chinese company to take its best technology to a place like Australia. We know these sorts of technology exports are scrutinised much more closely than in the past as economic exchanges have become more securitised.
In fact, China is ahead of Australia in areas such as artificial intelligence and robotics. And even in fundamental scientific research, China now produces more of the world’s best fundamental scientific publications than the US. It’s very impressive.
As an Australian, I do my best to raise awareness in Australia about the reality of the world in 2026. If Australia wants to stay at that technology frontier, we have to remain as deeply connected to China as we possibly can. I understand that every country has to protect its national security, but my view is that Australia needs to be engaged with China to the maximum extent possible.
CNS: The upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, China, and Australian Prime Minister Albanese will travel to China to attend. How do you view the opportunities for cooperation within the APEC framework?
James Laurenceson: The good thing about Australia and China is that when it comes to trade, which is primarily what APEC is about in terms of broader economic cooperation, the two countries are actually quite aligned. More trade and more economic integration aren't just good for prosperity; they're good for stability and security too. So that's a great starting point.
If a majority of APEC members take the opportunity at the November meeting in Shenzhen to simply signal that they remain committed to open and free global markets, I think that's a positive outcome.n is an economist, educator, analyst and researcher. He is Director of the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney.
Professor Laurenceson conducts research that seeks to inform Australia’s engagement with China. His research has been published in leading scholarly journals including China Economic Review, China Economic Journal, Journal of Contemporary China and Australian Journal of International Affairs.
Professor Laurenceson also provides regular commentary on contemporary developments in China’s economy and the Australia-China relationship. His opinion articles have appeared in The Australian Financial Review, The Australian, The Sydney Morning Herald, South China Morning Post, among many other publications.

（中新社）——近年来，澳中关系持续改善和发展，贸易和人文交流为双边关系发展提供了重要动力。然而，深化合作仍面临挑战，包括地缘政治紧张、战略认知差异以及研究合作相关问题。两国如何增进相互理解、扩大共同利益、管控分歧，将互补优势转化为更多实实在在的成果？在近日接受中国新闻社“W.E.对话”采访时，澳大利亚经济学家、悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究院院长詹姆斯·劳伦斯森强调了两国之间的深度互补性。

“我们必须尽可能与中国保持紧密联系，”他说，并强调澳大利亚需要最大限度地与中国接触与合作，“尽我们所能参与中国的发展”。以下是采访摘录：中新社：近年来，澳中关系重回稳步改善和发展的轨道。您如何看待这一关系的深层驱动力和未来前景？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：我持谨慎乐观态度。我认为双方都不希望回到2020年至2022年间澳中关系失调的状态。我也认为处理这一关系的方式相当积极且非常务实。

中国前驻澳大利亚大使肖千在澳任职四年半，最近才返回北京。他过去常在公开场合说，我们有分歧，甚至有争端。我并不认为这是负面的。我认为他非常坦率，这是积极的。

他还会紧接着说，双方都不希望这些争端和分歧蔓延开来，损害共同合作的领域。双方都认识到，尽管分歧确实存在，但我们也有巨大的共同利益。贸易是最明显的，但不仅限于贸易。例如，在多边组织方面，堪培拉和北京都是世界贸易组织的坚定支持者，双方继续开展合作。我期待澳中合作取得进一步进展。

中新社：悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究院自2014年成立以来，与中国高校和智库保持着非常活跃的交流。您认为人文交流，特别是智库交流，在促进双边关系中发挥什么作用？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：人文交流，特别是智库交流，发挥着重要作用，也有亮点。学者和专家在二轨层面会晤，能够进行更坦率的讨论。澳中关系研究院仍然非常热衷于与来访澳大利亚的中国代表团接触。

我们的许多员工，包括我本人，也经常去中国。我们需要这样做，因为尽管双边关系中有很多善意，但误解也可能产生。例如，我在中国经常遇到的一种观点是，澳大利亚总是自动跟随美国。我去中国时，可以举出许多澳大利亚与美国持完全不同立场的领域的例子。我认为这种不同的视角对双方都有好处。

贸易是最明显的例子。去年唐纳德·特朗普重新执政时，华盛顿传出一些言论，称华盛顿希望澳大利亚限制或削减与中国的贸易关系。澳大利亚贸易部长的回应是：“我们不想减少与中国的生意，我们想增加与中国的生意。我们将根据国家利益来决定如何继续与中国接触，而不是根据美国人可能想要或不想要什么。”这是一位澳大利亚部长非常大胆的表态。另一个例子是技术问题。

澳大利亚对中国电动汽车、电池和太阳能产品非常欢迎且完全开放，对这些产品征收零关税。事实上，就在今年，中国超越日本成为澳大利亚最大的汽车供应国，而日本占据这一位置近三十年。现在我们最大的来源是中国。同样，反过来也是如此。当中国同事来到澳大利亚时，他们可以给澳大利亚受众带来他们可能从未听过的观点。

所以这是积极的。我要对中国在免签政策上采取的举措表示肯定。这对前往中国的澳大利亚人显然有好处，对中国也确实有好处。更多澳大利亚人能够亲眼看到中国，这是好事。我希望澳大利亚政府能采取对等做法，但迄今尚未这样做。

中新社：我们注意到，您在最近的文章中指出，澳大利亚对与中国的研究合作采取过度限制的做法，有可能错失获得世界一流科学技术的机会。您如何评估两国保持开放科技合作的重要性？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：开放的科技合作至关重要。实际上，这对澳大利亚比对中国更重要。中国是一个大国，拥有大量人才。

坦率地说，如果澳大利亚不与中国合作，中国也不会有问题。中国目前拥有庞大的国内人力资本池。澳大利亚人口少、规模有限，一直更依赖国际合作。如果你看澳大利亚最高质量的科学出版物，大约80%涉及国际合作。一个像澳大利亚这样规模和资源的国家，要保持在国际技术前沿，唯一的途径就是开展国际合作。

另一方面，中国的创新体系和人才库在过去十年中发展巨大。如果我们与世界上领先的创新和人才来源隔绝，那将给澳大利亚带来巨大代价。这就是我的担忧。中新社：澳大利亚外长要求澳大利亚国立大学和昆士兰大学分别终止与山东大学和中国科学院的合作。您如何看待这一事态？

詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：我一直在密切关注这两则新闻。决策背后可能有我不了解的相关信息，但我可以谈两点。首先，至少从表面上看，这些交易似乎并不特别有风险。例如，山东大学与澳大利亚国立大学的协议主要是关于本科教学，甚至没有研究部分。

所以我不清楚这如何威胁到澳大利亚的利益或国家安全。同样，与昆士兰大学的协议也不是特别有风险的交易。所以我认为这引发了很多困惑。其次，其影响将是许多其他大学和学者会关注发生的事情，并自行评估出了什么问题。他们将不愿与中国缔结新的合作协议，因为他们担心，如果他们投入所有这些工作，以善意和诚信与中国伙伴接触，然后协议被取消，澳大利亚大学将陷入巨大混乱，中国伙伴也是如此。

双方可能甚至不会尝试。我认为这就是风险所在。中新社：您如何看待澳中在绿色领域，特别是清洁能源和新能源汽车方面的合作机遇？两国如何携手推进绿色经济、加强绿色合作？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：正如澳中经济关系的许多其他领域一样，两国就是有着深度的互补性。

这就是澳中经贸往来如此强劲的原因。仅举绿色领域的几个例子：澳大利亚是全球主要的锂供应国，中国是其最大的锂矿石出口市场。中国电动汽车在澳大利亚非常受欢迎，家用电池系统和太阳能电池板也是如此。双方可以采取一些措施将其提升到更高水平。如果我为澳大利亚政府提供建议，我会敦促其对中国在澳投资更加开放，特别是在可再生能源领域。

过去五年，澳大利亚政府对中国投资采取了更严格的做法，特别是在关键矿产等某些领域。我想不出过去五年中该领域有哪一项投资获得批准。我认为这是一个错误。这在安全方向上走得太远了，可能带来重大经济代价。澳大利亚可以从许多国家获得投资资本。

这并不难，但中国企业如今往往也是世界技术领导者。这就是外国投资的特点：不仅仅是美元，通常还捆绑着技术。我认为，如果我们完全阻止中国投资，对澳大利亚的利益将非常不利。还有一个问题是，北京是否允许中国公司将其最好的技术带到澳大利亚这样的地方。我们知道，随着经济交流日益安全化，这类技术出口比过去受到更严格的审查。

事实上，中国在人工智能和机器人等领域领先于澳大利亚。即使在基础科学研究方面，中国现在产生的世界最佳基础科学出版物也比美国多。这非常令人印象深刻。作为澳大利亚人，我尽我所能提高澳大利亚人对2026年世界现实的认识。如果澳大利亚想保持在技术前沿，我们必须尽可能与中国保持紧密联系。

我理解每个国家都必须保护其国家安全，但我的观点是，澳大利亚需要最大限度地与中国接触。中新社：即将举行的亚太经合组织领导人非正式会议将在中国深圳举行，澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯将赴华出席。您如何看待亚太经合组织框架内的合作机遇？詹姆斯·劳伦斯森：澳大利亚和中国的好处在于，在贸易方面——这基本上是亚太经合组织更广泛经济合作的主要内容——两国实际上相当一致。更多贸易和更深入的经济一体化不仅有利于繁荣，也有利于稳定和安全。

所以这是一个很好的起点。如果大多数亚太经合组织成员利用11月深圳会议的机会， simply表明他们仍然致力于开放和自由的全球市场，我认为这是一个积极的成果。劳伦斯森是一位经济学家、教育家、分析师和研究员。他是悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究院院长。劳伦斯森教授开展研究，旨在为澳大利亚与中国的接触提供参考。他的研究成果发表在《中国经济评论》《中国经济杂志》《当代中国杂志》和《澳大利亚国际事务杂志》等领先学术期刊上。

劳伦斯森教授还定期就中国经济和澳中关系的当代发展发表评论。他的评论文章发表在《澳大利亚金融评论》《澳大利亚人报》《悉尼先驱晨报》《南华早报》等众多出版物上。

articles.title: Xi calls for new achievements on new Long March at ceremony commemorating 90th anniversary of Long March victory
articles.titleCn: 习近平在纪念长征胜利90周年大会上号召在新长征路上争取新成就
articles.summary: A grand assembly marking the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army was held on the morning of Oct. 22 at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC), delivered an important speech. He stressed that only by remembering history can a brighter future be created. Xi urged the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee, carry forward the great spirit of the Long March, press ahead with renewed resolve and perseverance, advance the great cause pioneered by revolutionary predecessors, and strive for new achievements on the new Long March.
articles.summaryCn: 习近平在纪念长征胜利90周年大会上发表重要讲话，号召全党全军全国各族人民弘扬伟大长征精神，在新长征路上争取新成就。

paragraphs.en: A grand {{1}} marking the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army was held on the morning of Oct. 22 at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC), delivered an important speech. He stressed that only by remembering history can a brighter future be created. Xi urged the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee, carry forward the great spirit of the Long March, press ahead with renewed resolve and {{2}}, advance the great cause {{3}} by revolutionary predecessors, and strive for new achievements on the new Long March.
paragraphs.cn: 纪念中国工农红军长征胜利90周年大会于10月22日上午在北京人民大会堂隆重举行。中共中央总书记、国家主席、中央军委主席习近平发表重要讲话。他强调，只有铭记历史，才能创造更加光明的未来。习近平号召全党全军全国各族人民更加紧密地团结在党中央周围，弘扬伟大长征精神，以 renewed 决心和毅力奋勇前进，推进革命前辈开创的伟大事业，在新长征路上争取新成就。

paragraphs.en:
Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, attended the event. The atmosphere in the grand auditorium of the Great Hall of the People was {{4}} yet vibrant. Above the rostrum hung a banner reading "Commemorative Assembly on the 90th Anniversary of the Victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army." At the center of the backdrop gleamed the {{5}} emblem of the CPC, with the huge year numerals "1936-2026" beneath it, flanked by five red flags on each side. A long banner hung on the second-floor balcony read: "Unite closely around the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, carry forward the great spirit of the Long March, forge ahead on the new Long March, and strive tirelessly to comprehensively advance the great cause of building a strong country and achieving national {{6}} through Chinese modernization!"
At 10 a.m., Zhao Leji announced the start of the assembly. All present rose to their feet and sang the national anthem.
paragraphs.cn: 中共中央政治局常委李强、赵乐际、王沪宁、蔡奇、丁薛祥、李希，以及国家副主席韩正出席大会。人民大会堂大礼堂气氛庄重而热烈。主席台上方悬挂着“纪念中国工农红军长征胜利90周年大会”的横幅。背景中央是熠熠生辉的中国共产党党徽，下方是巨大的年份数字“1936-2026”，两侧各有五面红旗。二楼眺台上悬挂着长横幅：“紧密团结在以习近平同志为核心的党中央周围，全面贯彻习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想，弘扬伟大长征精神，在新长征路上奋勇前进，为以中国式现代化全面推进强国建设、民族复兴伟业而不懈奋斗！”上午10时，赵乐际宣布大会开始。全体起立，高唱国歌。

paragraphs.en: Amid enthusiastic applause, Xi delivered the speech. On behalf of the CPC Central Committee, the State Council, the CMC, the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups, he paid high {{7}} to Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and all the other veteran revolutionaries who led the Red Army in accomplishing the historic feat of the Long March; to the Red Army commanders and soldiers who fought {{8}} through bloodshed during the Long March and who continued fighting in various parts of the country; to the people of all ethnic groups who aided the Red Army on its Long March, especially those in revolutionary base areas; and to all surviving Red Army veterans. At Xi's proposal, all attendees rose and observed a moment of silence for all fallen heroes of the Long March and of revolutionary struggles across China. From October 1934 to October 1936, under the leadership of the CPC, the Red Army's first, second, and fourth front armies, as well as the 25th Army, carried out the great Long March that Xi said stunned the world and is etched in history. During the Long March, the Red Army traversed more than 10 provinces and marched as far as 12,500 kilometers, fighting their way out of the {{9}}, interceptions and pursuit by more than 1 million enemy troops.
paragraphs.cn: 在热烈的掌声中，习近平发表讲话。他代表党中央、国务院、中央军委，代表全党全军全国各族人民，向领导红军创造长征历史伟绩的毛泽东、周恩来、朱德等老一辈革命家，向在长征中浴血奋战、在全国各地坚持斗争的红军指战员，向支援红军长征的各族人民特别是革命根据地人民，向所有健在的红军老战士，致以崇高敬意。在习近平提议下，全体与会人员起立，为在长征途中和在各地革命斗争中英勇牺牲的革命先烈默哀。习近平说，从1934年10月到1936年10月，在中国共产党领导下，红军第一、第二、第四方面军和红二十五军进行了震惊世界、彪炳史册的伟大长征。长征途中，红军跨越10多个省，行程最远达12500公里，冲破百万敌军的围追堵截。

paragraphs.en: The victory of the Long March declared the total failure of the Kuomintang reactionaries' attempts to {{10}} the CPC and the Red Army. Xi stressed that revisiting history is about drawing wisdom and strength from it to forge ahead.

paragraphs.en: "Ninety years on, as we once again look back on that grueling yet glorious journey, we have come to understand more profoundly that the victory of the Long March was {{13}}, as it embodied the way by which the Party and the people's army marched toward victory with firm and {{14}} steps," Xi said. Xi said that this great road to victory was blazed by relying on the Party's right leadership. The Party's right leadership and the establishment of Comrade Mao Zedong's core position were of decisive significance to the victory of the Red Army's Long March. This great road to victory was forged by relying on firm revolutionary will. paragraphs.cn: 习近平说：“90年过去了，当我们再次回顾那段艰苦卓绝而又光辉的历程，我们更加深刻地认识到，长征的胜利是必然的，因为它体现了党和人民军队以坚定果敢的步伐走向胜利的道路。”习近平说，这条伟大胜利之路，是靠党的正确领导开辟的。党的正确领导和毛泽东同志核心地位的确立，对红军长征的胜利具有决定性意义。这条伟大胜利之路，是靠坚定的革命意志锻造的。革命理想信念能够迸发出无穷的力量，足以战胜顽固的敌人、撼动高山，一支充满崇高理想和坚定信念的军队是不可战胜的。

paragraphs.en: This great road to victory was pioneered with the spirit of independence, self-reliance, and seeking truth from facts. Only when the basic tenets of Marxism are closely integrated with China's specific realities can they resolve problems in China and demonstrate their strong {{16}}. This great road to victory was opened up by relying on the support of the broad masses of the people, who are always the source of strength and the {{17}} backing of the Party and the people's army. "As long as we take deep root among the people and always maintain flesh-and-blood ties with them, the Party's cause will advance from victory to victory," Xi said. Xi noted that the Red Army's Long March was an extraordinary miracle in human history and forged the great Long March spirit.
paragraphs.cn: 这条伟大胜利之路，是靠独立自主、实事求是的精神开创的。只有把马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际紧密结合，才能解决中国的问题，才能展现出强大的生命力。这条伟大胜利之路，是靠广大人民群众的支持开辟的，人民群众始终是党和人民军队的力量源泉和坚强后盾。习近平说：“只要我们深深扎根于人民之中，始终同人民保持血肉联系，党的事业就会从胜利走向胜利。”习近平指出，红军长征是人类历史上的非凡奇迹，锻造了伟大的长征精神。

A grand assembly marking the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army was held on the morning of Oct. 22 at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC), delivered an important speech. He stressed that only by remembering history can a brighter future be created. Xi urged the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee, carry forward the great spirit of the Long March, press ahead with renewed resolve and perseverance, advance the great cause pioneered by revolutionary predecessors, and strive for new achievements on the new Long March.
Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, attended the event.
The atmosphere in the grand auditorium of the Great Hall of the People was solemn yet vibrant. Above the rostrum hung a banner reading "Commemorative Assembly on the 90th Anniversary of the Victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army." At the center of the backdrop gleamed the radiant emblem of the CPC, with the huge year numerals "1936-2026" beneath it, flanked by five red flags on each side. A long banner hung on the second-floor balcony read: "Unite closely around the Party Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core, fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, carry forward the great spirit of the Long March, forge ahead on the new Long March, and strive tirelessly to comprehensively advance the great cause of building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization!"
At 10 a.m., Zhao Leji announced the start of the assembly. All present rose to their feet and sang the national anthem.
Amid enthusiastic applause, Xi delivered the speech. On behalf of the CPC Central Committee, the State Council, the CMC, the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups, he paid high tribute to Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Zhu De and all the other veteran revolutionaries who led the Red Army in accomplishing the historic feat of the Long March; to the Red Army commanders and soldiers who fought valiantly through bloodshed during the Long March and who continued fighting in various parts of the country; to the people of all ethnic groups who aided the Red Army on its Long March, especially those in revolutionary base areas; and to all surviving Red Army veterans. At Xi's proposal, all attendees rose and observed a moment of silence for all fallen heroes of the Long March and of revolutionary struggles across China.
From October 1934 to October 1936, under the leadership of the CPC, the Red Army's first, second, and fourth front armies, as well as the 25th Army, carried out the great Long March that Xi said stunned the world and is etched in history. During the Long March, the Red Army traversed more than 10 provinces and marched as far as 12,500 kilometers, fighting their way out of the encirclement, interceptions and pursuit by more than 1 million enemy troops. The victory of the Long March declared the total failure of the Kuomintang reactionaries' attempts to annihilate the CPC and the Red Army. It marked the Red Army's successful strategic transfer northward to resist Japanese aggression, which opened up a new phase in the Chinese revolution. "This earth-shattering revolutionary feat holds great significance in the history of our Party, country and military, and has a profound impact on our path toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. This stirring heroic epic will forever be engraved on the monument of the Chinese revolution and remembered by hundreds of millions of people," Xi noted.
Xi stressed that revisiting history is about drawing wisdom and strength from it to forge ahead. "Ninety years on, as we once again look back on that grueling yet glorious journey, we have come to understand more profoundly that the victory of the Long March was inevitable, as it embodied the way by which the Party and the people's army marched toward victory with firm and resolute steps," Xi said.
Xi said that this great road to victory was blazed by relying on the Party's right leadership. The Party's right leadership and the establishment of Comrade Mao Zedong's core position were of decisive significance to the victory of the Red Army's Long March. This great road to victory was forged by relying on firm revolutionary will. Revolutionary ideals and convictions can unleash boundless strength capable of defeating stubborn enemies and shaking mountains, and an army imbued with lofty ideals and firm convictions is invincible. This great road to victory was pioneered with the spirit of independence, self-reliance, and seeking truth from facts. Only when the basic tenets of Marxism are closely integrated with China's specific realities can they resolve problems in China and demonstrate their strong vitality. This great road to victory was opened up by relying on the support of the broad masses of the people, who are always the source of strength and the steadfast backing of the Party and the people's army. "As long as we take deep root among the people and always maintain flesh-and-blood ties with them, the Party's cause will advance from victory to victory," Xi said.
Xi noted that the Red Army's Long March was an extraordinary miracle in human history and forged the great Long March spirit. Where there is spirit, there is strength. The great spirit of the Long March fully demonstrates the power of loyalty, truth, justice and solidarity. "As an important part of the spiritual pedigree of the Chinese Communists, the spirit transcends time and space, retains its vitality over time, and will always be a precious treasure and a powerful force inspiring us to overcome difficulties and forge ahead courageously," Xi said.
Xi emphasized that the history of the Long March has never receded into the distant past, and the road of the Long March continues to extend. Over the 90 years since the victory of the Long March, the Party has united and led the people in undertaking one great Long March after another and winning one great victory after another across all historical periods of revolution, construction, and reform. Since the 18th CPC National Congress, socialism with Chinese characteristics has entered a new era. Through the concerted efforts of the entire Party, the military, and Chinese people of all ethnic groups, the First Centenary Goal of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects has been realized on schedule. The cause of the Party and the country has achieved historic accomplishments and undergone historic transformations. On the new journey, we are now committed to realizing the Second Centenary Goal of building China into a great modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through Chinese modernization, Xi said.
Xi noted that the new journey is a long expedition filled with glory and dreams, and is a new Long March for the Party and the people. He said that to carry forward the great spirit of the Long March and make steady progress on the new Long March, it is imperative to:
-- stay committed to the Party's ideals, convictions and fundamental purpose, fully implement the Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, remain true to the Party's original aspiration and founding mission, and rely closely on the people to create new historic achievements;
-- unswervingly advance high-quality development, continuously meet the people's ever-growing needs for a better life, ensure coordinated implementation of the Five-Sphere Integrated Plan and the Four-Pronged Comprehensive Strategy, promote higher-quality economic growth while achieving an appropriate increase in economic output, and advance common prosperity for all;
-- have the courage to carry out a great struggle with many new historical features, better ensure both development and security, and seize the historical initiative to overcome difficulties, combat risks and meet challenges, so as to ensure that the giant ship of national rejuvenation cuts through the waves and sails steadily forward;
-- accelerate reinforcing the people's armed forces to world-class standards, always uphold the Party's absolute leadership over the army, realize the goals for the centenary of the People's Liberation Army on schedule, and advance national defense and military modernization with high quality;
-- uphold Party leadership, strengthen Party building, persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance, and consistently advance its efforts to purify, improve, renew, and excel itself, ensuring that the Party serves as the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics.
While presiding over the event, Zhao Leji said Xi's important speech reviewed the great course of the Red Army's Long March led by the Party, summarized the great significance of the victory of the Long March, revealed the key to victory that has enabled the Party and the people's army to march forward resolutely, expounded the historical value of the great Long March spirit, and set out clear requirements for carrying forward the great Long March spirit and succeeding in the new Long March. Xi's speech was of immense political, ideological and guiding significance, Zhao said, urging earnest efforts to study and grasp its essence and ensure its effective implementation. He called on the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core, follow the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, gain a profound understanding of the decisive significance of the "Two Affirmations," strengthen the "Four Consciousnesses," bolster the "Four Confidences," and ensure the "Two Upholds." He urged efforts to carry forward the great spirit of the Long March, succeed in the new Long March, and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization.
The assembly concluded to the powerful strains of The Internationale.
The event was attended by members of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, members of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, vice chairperson of the CMC, vice chairpersons of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, state councilors, the president of the Supreme People's Court, and vice chairpersons of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, who were in Beijing.
Also in attendance were about 3,000 people, including leading officials of central Party and government departments, the military, people's organizations, and the Beijing municipal government; leaders of non-CPC political parties' central committees and the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce; representatives of personages without party affiliation; representatives of retired officials; representatives of officers and soldiers of the People's Liberation Army and the People's Armed Police Force; and representatives of people from all walks of life in the capital.

这条伟大胜利之路，是靠独立自主、实事求是的精神开创的。只有把马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际紧密结合，才能解决中国的问题，才能展现出强大的生命力。这条伟大胜利之路，是靠广大人民群众的支持开辟的，人民群众始终是党和人民军队的力量源泉和坚强后盾。习近平说：“只要我们深深扎根于人民之中，始终同人民保持血肉联系，党的事业就会从胜利走向胜利。”习近平指出，红军长征是人类历史上的非凡奇迹，锻造了伟大的长征精神。

articles.fullText:
(ECNS) -- "Our entire family is Tibetan, and we have always spoken the Tibetan language within our family. Originally, our family had no Han surname. But my grandfather said that we must engrave the Red Army's kindness forever in our family's name and let it forever flow in our blood," recalled Ma Hua, a museum instructor at Baoxing County, Ya'an City, Southwest China's Sichuan Province.
The Han surname of the Ma family begins with Ma Hua's grandfather, Teba who served as a guide for the Red Army. He was one of the guides when the Red Army crossed Jiajin Mountain during the Long March.
In June 1935, the Red Army's advance unit reached Qiaoqi (today's Qiaoqi Tibetan Township) in Baoxing County, at the southern foot of Jiajin Mountain. Influenced by hostile propaganda, local residents were panic-stricken and fled into the mountains. But Teba, then only 15, could not help wondering: How was this army different from other armies? To this end, Teba came back down from the mountain to the village.
At that time, Jiajin Mountain was battered by the wind and snow. Jiajin Mountain at Baoxing County, stretches across the border between Baoxing County, Ya'an City, Sichuan Province, and Maogong County (today's Xiaojin County) in Aba Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture. It is a key strategic pass linking the Chengdu Plain in western Sichuan with the northwestern Sichuan Plateau. The mountain's Tibetan name is "Jiaji," meaning "very high and very steep."
It was on this high, steep, and treacherous snowy mountain that the Red Army was about to embark on one of the most perilous crossings of the Long March, and it was here that young Teba was about to forge an enduring bond with this army.
"After observing the soldiers, my grandfather found that although the Red Army soldiers were hungry and cold, they were a highly disciplined force that loved and helped the people. They did not enter local residents' homes, actively protected monasteries, took no food from Tibetan households, and did not take even a needle or thread from the Tibetan people," Ma Hua said.
At the same time, her grandfather immediately understood that the Red Army was an army fighting to win the world for the poor.
Teba was familiar with the local terrain. On that year, he alone led the Red Army across the Jiajin Mountain. During this period, Teba made repeated trips between the southern and northern slopes of the mountain, helping the main forces of the Central Red Army cross the snow-capped mountain one after another. As they were about to part, a Red Army soldier gave Teba a kerosene lantern and gave him a Han Chinese name—"Ma Denghong."
"This lamp was also meant to wish my grandfather a safe journey back. The lamps back then were kerosene lamps, and the wick could be adjusted larger or smaller at any time. Crossing Jiajin Mountain took nearly a whole day; without any light along the way, one risked missing a step," Ma Hua explained.
From then on, her grandfather treasured the lamp very much and took "Ma" as his surname, which the family has used ever since.
Ma Hua never met her grandfather, but she has walked the road he once took with her own feet since childhood.
"During the years I was in middle and high school, my father and mother took me to cross Jiajin Mountain, following the route the Red Army took, all the way to Dawei in Xiaojin County. The first time I crossed Jiajin Mountain, my nose bled. I was young then, and my skin was tender; after climbing for a day, the skin on my face peeled. My father was rather strict. I don't know where he got a long rope, but he tied it around my waist and pulled me from the front, while my mother followed alongside," Ma Hua recalled.
"People often say, 'if you want to know what hardship is, think of the Red Army's 25,000-li Long March.' My father rarely preached principles, instead, he influenced us through the little things in daily life."
For Ma Hua, only by walking on the snow-covered mountain trails can heself understand what that lamp had meant in the darkness. Crossing Jiajin Mountain was more like a special rite of growing up.
Today, Ma Hua continues to share her grandfather's story with the world. The lamp with which Teba once guided the Red Army through wind and snow is now carried on by his granddaughter, lighting the way for those who come after.

“当时的灯是煤油灯，灯芯随时可以调大调小。翻越夹金山需要将近一整天；一路上没有光，就可能踩空，”马花解释道。从那以后，她的爷爷非常珍视这盏灯，并以“马”为姓，这个姓氏从此被家族沿用。马花从未见过她的爷爷，但她从小就用自己的双脚走过他曾经走过的路。“在我上初中和高中的那些年，我的父母带我翻越夹金山，沿着红军走过的路线，一直走到小金县的达维。

“我第一次翻越夹金山时，鼻子流血了。那时我还小，皮肤娇嫩；爬了一天后，我脸上的皮肤脱落了。我父亲相当严格。我不知道他从哪里弄来一根长绳，把它系在我的腰上，从前面拉我，而我母亲跟在旁边，”马花回忆道。“人们常说，‘要想知道什么是艰苦，就想想红军的两万五千里长征。’我父亲很少讲大道理，而是通过日常生活中的小事影响我们。”对马花来说，只有走在白雪覆盖的山路上，她自己才能理解那盏灯在黑暗中意味着什么。

翻越夹金山更像是一种特殊的成长仪式。如今，马花继续向世界讲述她爷爷的故事。特巴曾经用来引导红军穿越风雪的那盏灯，现在由他的孙女提着，为后来者照亮道路。

articles.fullText:
China's clean energy equipment industry has made significant progress in technological innovation, industrial scale and international market expansion this year, providing strong support for the global energy transition, according to the China Machinery Industry Federation (CMIF).
China's total installed power generation capacity reached 4.103 billion kilowatts by the end of August, up 11.1% year on year, reflecting continued growth in the country's energy infrastructure.
In the first half of this year, output of nuclear power, hydropower and wind power generating units increased 92%, 51.9% and 11.5% year on year, respectively, the CMIF said.
On October 13, Dongfang Electric Machinery, based in Deyang, Sichuan Province, dispatched a batch of gas, hydropower and wind power equipment for energy projects in several Chinese provinces.
The equipment features domestically developed key materials, core manufacturing processes and advanced hydraulic and electromagnetic designs, helping overcome technological bottlenecks and strengthen China's independent manufacturing capabilities.
Meanwhile, new energy storage technologies are moving from demonstration projects toward large-scale deployment. A phase-change direct-cooling system developed for energy storage applications can improve heat transfer efficiency, enhance battery temperature uniformity, reduce auxiliary energy consumption and mitigate thermal runaway risks.
China has also achieved breakthroughs in emerging energy technologies, including the engineering application of vanadium redox flow batteries and advances in key hydrogen energy materials and equipment.
Overseas markets drive growth
Overseas demand has become an increasingly important growth engine for China's clean energy equipment industry, with exports of power generation, transmission and transformation, and energy storage equipment maintaining strong momentum.
Recently, an F-class 50-megawatt heavy-duty gas turbine departed from Deyang for Kazakhstan via the Horgos port. The shipment marked the first overseas export of a fully domestically manufactured high-end heavy-duty gas turbine as a complete unit.
In September, Tanzania's Julius Nyerere Hydropower Station officially entered commercial operation. With a total installed capacity of 2,115 megawatts, the project represents the largest hydropower project exported in a single package under a Chinese proprietary brand. Its annual power generation has exceeded 3.1 billion kilowatt-hours, helping meet approximately half of Tanzania's electricity demand.
Industry experts said China's clean energy equipment exports are shifting from individual products toward integrated solutions combining technology, standards and services.
China has cooperated with more than 100 countries and regions on green energy projects. Chinese manufacturers supply around 70% of the world's wind power equipment and 80% of its photovoltaic modules, with clean energy products reaching more than 200 countries and regions.
Innovation underpins high-quality development
At the 2026 World Conference on Clean Energy Equipment, held in Deyang, participants highlighted innovation and intelligent manufacturing as key drivers of high-quality industrial development.
At Dongfang Electric Machinery's digital welding workshop, automated production lines have shortened product design cycles by 40% and manufacturing cycles by 30%. The company's first-pass product qualification rate has remained above 98%.
According to China's 15th Five-Year Plan for the development of a new energy system, the country's total installed power capacity is expected to reach 5.4 billion kilowatts by 2030, with wind and solar power accounting for more than half of the total.
Industry leaders called for deeper integration of artificial intelligence and advanced digital technologies with equipment manufacturing, stronger domestic capabilities in core materials and components, and forward-looking investment in energy storage, hydrogen energy and controlled nuclear fusion.
These efforts are expected to strengthen China's energy equipment industry and create new opportunities for international cooperation in the global transition toward cleaner energy.

articles.title: China’s rural revival: How a cliffside village defies isolation
articles.titleCn: 中国乡村振兴：悬崖村如何打破与世隔绝
articles.summary: For generations, rural communities across Africa have watched their young people leave in search of better opportunities in cities. But in a remote mountain village in southwestern China, a different story is unfolding–one built around connecting communities, improving livelihoods and making rural life more viable.
articles.summaryCn: 文章通过四川古路村的蜕变，展示中国乡村振兴如何以基础设施连接偏远社区，并引发对非洲农村能否让年轻人留下的思考。

paragraphs.en: For generations, rural communities across Africa have watched their young people leave in search of better opportunities in cities. But in a {{0}} mountain village in southwestern China, a different story is unfolding–one built around connecting communities, improving livelihoods and making rural life more {{1}}. In Gulu Village, in Sichuan Province, a 750-meter cableway stretches across a deep mountain gorge, offering residents a vital link to the outside world. What might appear to visitors as a scenic attraction has become a symbol of the village’s transformation. When I travelled from Kenya to Gulu, I wanted to understand how China’s rural {{2}} efforts are changing life in communities far removed from its {{3}} cities and modern skylines.
paragraphs.cn: 世代以来，非洲各地的农村社区目睹着年轻人离开家乡，前往城市寻找更好的机会。但在中国西南部一个偏远山村，一个不同的故事正在展开——一个围绕连接社区、改善生计和让农村生活更可行的故事。在四川省古路村，一条750米长的索道横跨深山谷地，为居民提供了通往外界的生命线。在游客看来可能只是景点的索道，已成为村庄转型的象征。当我从肯尼亚来到古路村时，我想了解中国的乡村振兴努力如何改变那些远离其 sprawling 城市和现代天际线的社区的生活。

paragraphs.en:
Gulu village {{4}} on mountain cliffs in Sichuan Province, China. Africa
The journey revealed a {{5}} contrast between the village’s past and present. According to the village head Zheng Wangchun, residents once faced enormous challenges accessing basic services. Before roads and safer routes reached the area, journeys down the mountain could take days. Children walked for hours to school, healthcare was difficult to access, and many families struggled with {{6}} housing, food and electricity.
paragraphs.cn: 古路村坐落在陡峭的山崖上，位于中国四川省。非洲。这段旅程揭示了村庄过去与现在的鲜明对比。据村长郑望春介绍，居民曾经在获取基本服务方面面临巨大挑战。在道路和更安全的路线到达该地区之前，下山可能需要数天时间。孩子们步行数小时上学，医疗难以获得，许多家庭在住房、食物和电力方面捉襟见肘。

paragraphs.en: Progress came gradually. A narrow mountain path built in 2003 offered an alternative to dangerous routes along the cliffs. A road reached the area in 2009, while the cableway began operating in 2018, helping overcome some of the geographical {{7}} that had isolated the community. Today, tunnels and bridges connect settlements across the mountainous landscape, while {{8}} projects have helped improve access to {{9}} services. A pipeline stretching nearly five kilometers brings water to residents, addressing a need that was once difficult to meet.
paragraphs.cn: 进步是逐步到来的。2003年修建的一条狭窄山路为悬崖上的危险路线提供了替代选择。2009年，一条公路通到了该地区，而索道于2018年开始运营，帮助克服了曾使该社区与世隔绝的一些地理障碍。如今，隧道和桥梁连接着山区各地的定居点，基础设施项目也帮助改善了基本服务的获取。一条近五公里长的管道为居民引来了水，满足了曾经难以满足的需求。

paragraphs.en:
Tourists climb the mountainous Gulu village. Africa
But Gulu’s transformation is not just about roads, bridges and cable cars. It is also about creating economic opportunities. Local farmer Lan Xuan says improved transport links have brought more visitors to the area, creating new opportunities to sell local produce and specialties. She says tourists from major Chinese cities are increasingly discovering the village, with social media helping to attract visitors.
paragraphs.cn: 游客攀登古路村的山地。非洲。但古路村的转变不仅仅是道路、桥梁和缆车。它还关乎创造经济机会。当地农民兰轩说，改善的交通联系为该地区带来了更多游客，创造了销售当地农产品和特产的新机会。她说，来自中国大城市的游客越来越多地发现这个村庄，社交媒体帮助吸引了游客。

paragraphs.en: For communities seeking {{10}} livelihoods, the hope is that better {{11}} can generate income and give residents more reasons to remain in their hometowns. Yet challenges remain. Resident Xiang Yucai points to an {{12}} population, with many young people having moved to cities with their families. Better infrastructure has improved living conditions, but reversing urbanemigration remains a more complex task. Cable cars glide as they move tourists between the cliffs of Gulu village.
paragraphs.cn: 对于寻求可持续生计的社区来说，希望在于更好的连通性能够创造收入，并给居民更多理由留在家乡。然而挑战依然存在。居民向玉才指出人口老龄化问题，许多年轻人已随家人迁往城市。更好的基础设施改善了生活条件，但扭转人口外流仍是一项更为复杂的任务。缆车滑行着，在古路村的悬崖之间运送游客。

paragraphs.en:
Africa
Gulu’s experience offers a glimpse into China’s broader rural revitalization strategy, which seeks to connect infrastructure development with agriculture, rural industries, public services and improved livelihoods. For generations, rural communities across Africa have watched their young people leave in search of better opportunities in cities. But in a remote mountain village in southwestern China, a different story is unfolding–one built around connecting communities, improving livelihoods and making rural life more viable.
In Gulu Village, in Sichuan Province, a 750-meter cableway stretches across a deep mountain gorge, offering residents a vital link to the outside world. What might appear to visitors as a scenic attraction has become a symbol of the village’s transformation.
When I travelled from Kenya to Gulu, I wanted to understand how China’s rural revitalization efforts are changing life in communities far removed from its sprawling cities and modern skylines.
Gulu village perched on mountain cliffs in Sichuan Province, China. 
 Africa
The journey revealed a dramatic contrast between the village’s past and present.
According to the village head Zheng Wangchun, residents once faced enormous challenges accessing basic services. Before roads and safer routes reached the area, journeys down the mountain could take days. Children walked for hours to school, healthcare was difficult to access, and many families struggled with inadequate housing, food and electricity.
Progress came gradually.
A narrow mountain path built in 2003 offered an alternative to dangerous routes along the cliffs. A road reached the area in 2009, while the cableway began operating in 2018, helping overcome some of the geographical barriers that had isolated the community.
Today, tunnels and bridges connect settlements across the mountainous landscape, while infrastructure projects have helped improve access to essential services.
A pipeline stretching nearly five kilometers brings water to residents, addressing a need that was once difficult to meet.
Tourists climb the mountainous Gulu village. 
 Africa
But Gulu’s transformation is not just about roads, bridges and cable cars. It is also about creating economic opportunities.
Local farmer Lan Xuan says improved transport links have brought more visitors to the area, creating new opportunities to sell local produce and specialties. She says tourists from major Chinese cities are increasingly discovering the village, with social media helping to attract visitors.
For communities seeking sustainable livelihoods, the hope is that better connectivity can generate income and give residents more reasons to remain in their hometowns.
Yet challenges remain.
Resident Xiang Yucai points to an ageing population, with many young people having moved to cities with their families. Better infrastructure has improved living conditions, but reversing urbanemigration remains a more complex task.
Cable cars glide as they move tourists between the cliffs of Gulu village. 
 Africa
Gulu’s experience offers a glimpse into China’s broader rural revitalization strategy, which seeks to connect infrastructure development with agriculture, rural industries, public services and improved livelihoods.
As an African journalist, the journey raised a question that extends far beyond China: Can rural communities become places of opportunity rather than places people feel compelled to leave?
Across Africa, many villages face similar challenges, including poor infrastructure, limited access to healthcare and education, and inadequate economic opportunities. While the circumstances differ, Gulu offers an opportunity to examine how targeted investments in connectivity and local industries can help address some of these barriers.
The mountains surrounding Gulu have not changed. What has changed is how people navigate them and the possibilities that better connections can create.
Thousands of kilometers away, the same question remains relevant to rural Africa: what would it take to make village life a viable choice for the next generation?

世代以来，非洲各地的农村社区目睹着年轻人离开家乡，前往城市寻找更好的机会。但在中国西南部一个偏远山村，一个不同的故事正在展开——一个围绕连接社区、改善生计和让农村生活更可行的故事。在四川省古路村，一条750米长的索道横跨深山谷地，为居民提供了通往外界的生命线。在游客看来可能只是景点的索道，已成为村庄转型的象征。当我从肯尼亚来到古路村时，我想了解中国的乡村振兴努力如何改变那些远离其 sprawling 城市和现代天际线的社区的生活。

古路村坐落在陡峭的山崖上，位于中国四川省。非洲。这段旅程揭示了村庄过去与现在的鲜明对比。据村长郑望春介绍，居民曾经在获取基本服务方面面临巨大挑战。在道路和更安全的路线到达该地区之前，下山可能需要数天时间。孩子们步行数小时上学，医疗难以获得，许多家庭在住房、食物和电力方面捉襟见肘。

进步是逐步到来的。2003年修建的一条狭窄山路为悬崖上的危险路线提供了替代选择。2009年，一条公路通到了该地区，而索道于2018年开始运营，帮助克服了曾使该社区与世隔绝的一些地理障碍。如今，隧道和桥梁连接着山区各地的定居点，基础设施项目也帮助改善了基本服务的获取。一条近五公里长的管道为居民引来了水，满足了曾经难以满足的需求。

游客攀登古路村的山地。非洲。但古路村的转变不仅仅是道路、桥梁和缆车。它还关乎创造经济机会。当地农民兰轩说，改善的交通联系为该地区带来了更多游客，创造了销售当地农产品和特产的新机会。她说，来自中国大城市的游客越来越多地发现这个村庄，社交媒体帮助吸引了游客。

对于寻求可持续生计的社区来说，希望在于更好的连通性能够创造收入，并给居民更多理由留在家乡。然而挑战依然存在。居民向玉才指出人口老龄化问题，许多年轻人已随家人迁往城市。更好的基础设施改善了生活条件，但扭转人口外流仍是一项更为复杂的任务。缆车滑行着，在古路村的悬崖之间运送游客。

非洲。古路村的经验让人一窥中国更广泛的乡村振兴战略，该战略寻求将基础设施发展与农业、农村产业、公共服务和改善生计联系起来。作为一名非洲记者，这段旅程提出了一个远远超出中国的问题：农村社区能否成为充满机会的地方，而不是人们感到被迫离开的地方？在整个非洲，许多村庄面临类似的挑战，包括基础设施薄弱、医疗和教育机会有限，以及经济机会不足。尽管情况不同，古路村提供了一个机会，来审视对连通性和地方产业的有针对性投资如何帮助解决其中一些障碍。环绕古路村的群山没有改变。
